learning_objectives: Choose c’è for singular existence and ci sono for plural existence.
Form basic negative and yes/no existence sentences.
Describe what is present in a familiar place with short A1 sentences.

skills.description_en: Use c’è when one person or thing exists or is present.
Use ci sono when more than one person or thing exists or is present.
Form basic negative existential statements with non c’è and non ci sono.
Form basic existence questions with C’è...? and Ci sono...?.
Use c’è and ci sono in short familiar location phrases.
Produce short A1 sentences describing what is or is not present in a place.

lesson.short_explanation_en: Use c’è to say that one person or thing exists or is present, and ci sono for more than one: C’è un letto; Ci sono due sedie. For negation, put non before the form: non c’è, non ci sono. For yes/no questions, the form stays the same and the question mark/intonation marks the question: C’è un bagno? Ci sono due camere? C’è is written with an apostrophe and the accented verb form è. In this lesson, ci is part of the existential construction; its later pronominal uses are not introduced yet.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: The number of the person or thing presented determines the form.
rule_blocks.pattern: c’è + singular noun phrase / ci sono + plural noun phrase
usage_notes_en: Use c’è with one person or thing.
Use ci sono with two or more people or things.
The location phrase can come before or after the existential expression.
common_errors_en: Do not use c’è with a plural noun phrase.
Do not use ci sono with a singular noun phrase.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: Put non before the existential form to make a negative. A yes/no question uses the same c’è or ci sono form, with question intonation in speech and a question mark in writing.
rule_blocks.pattern: non c’è / non ci sono; C’è ...? / Ci sono ...?
usage_notes_en: Non ci sono is plural negative.
Do not add an English-style do/does auxiliary.
common_errors_en: Non follows neither c’è nor ci sono; it comes before them.
A plural question still uses ci sono.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: The singular form is written c’è, representing ci + è. It has an apostrophe after c and a grave accent on è.
usage_notes_en: Write c’è, not ce or cè.
Ci sono is written as two words.
common_errors_en: Ce is a different form and is not the existential verb phrase c’è.
The verb è requires its accent.
